lesson_scope: Modulus and principal argument definitions, polar and exponential representations, angle addition and subtraction under multiplication/division, principal argument range (-pi, pi], trigonometric deduction of exact surds, and geometric rotations in the Argand plane.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Direct calculation of modulus and principal argument in Quadrant 2.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding exact modulus and argument in Quadrant 2.

hints: Note that $x = -1 < 0$ and $y = \sqrt{3} > 0$, so $u$ lies in Quadrant 2.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the principal argument $\arg(u)$:
$$\text{Reference angle } \alpha = \arctan(\sqrt{3}) = \frac{\pi}{3}$$
Since $x < 0$ and $y > 0$ (Quadrant 2):
$$\arg(u) = \pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Modulus and argument in Quadrant 3.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding modulus and argument in Quadrant 3.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the principal argument $\arg(w)$ in Quadrant 3:
$$\alpha = \arctan(1) = \frac{\pi}{4}$$
$$\arg(w) = -\pi + \frac{\pi}{4} = -\frac{3\pi}{4}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Converting two numbers to exponential form with exact values.
Finding product in both polar and Cartesian forms.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate modulus and argument of $z w$:
$$|z w| = \sqrt{2} \times 6 = 6\sqrt{2}$$
$$\arg(z w) = -\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{2\pi}{3} = \frac{5\pi}{12}$$

Multiply in Cartesian form using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$:
$$z w = (1 - \mathrm{i})(-3 + 3\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}) = -3 + 3\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i} + 3\mathrm{i} - 3\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}^2$$
$$z w = (3\sqrt{3} - 3) + (3\sqrt{3} + 3)\mathrm{i}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Deducing exact trigonometric values of 5pi/12 from complex product.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Equating real parts to deduce exact cosine of composite angle.

hints: Multiply numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{2}$ to obtain $\frac{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}{4}$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the real parts of polar and Cartesian forms:
$$6\sqrt{2}\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right) = 3\sqrt{3} - 3 = 3(\sqrt{3} - 1)$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Equating imaginary parts and forming exact tangent.

hints: Multiply numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}$ to obtain $\frac{8 + 4\sqrt{3}}{4} = 2 + \sqrt{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Compute $\tan\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right)$ as the ratio of sine to cosine:
$$\tan\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Quotient properties and exact trigonometric values of 7pi/12.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding modulus and argument of fraction using quotient laws.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the moduli and arguments of numerator and denominator:
$$\text{Numerator: } |1 + \mathrm{i}\sqrt{3}| = 2, \quad \arg(1 + \mathrm{i}\sqrt{3}) = \frac{\pi}{3}$$
$$\text{Denominator: } |1 - \mathrm{i}| = \sqrt{2}, \quad \arg(1 - \mathrm{i}) = -\frac{\pi}{4}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Rationalising fraction and equating to deduce exact trigonometric ratios.

walkthrough.text:
Equate real and imaginary parts to polar form $z = \sqrt{2}\left(\cos\frac{7\pi}{12} + \mathrm{i}\sin\frac{7\pi}{12}\right)$:
$$\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{12}\right) = \frac{1 - \sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{6}}{4}$$
$$\sin\left(\frac{7\pi}{12}\right) = \frac{1 + \sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}}{4}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Multiplies numerator and denominator by $1 + \mathrm{i}$ and evaluates denominator as $2$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Polar half-angle identity application and modulus/argument deduction.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Applying half-angle exponential identity to numerator and denominator.

walkthrough.text:
Apply identity to the denominator with $\alpha = -\frac{\pi}{7}$:
$$\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\pi}{7}\mathrm{i}} - 1 = 2\mathrm{i}\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{14}\right)\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\pi}{14}\mathrm{i}} = -2\mathrm{i}\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{14}\right)\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\pi}{14}\mathrm{i}}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Deducing exact argument and modulus from ratio.

hints: Modulus is the ratio of positive sines: $|u| = \frac{\sin(2\pi/7)}{\sin(\pi/14)}$.
Due to the negative factor, subtract $\pi$: $\frac{5\pi}{14} - \pi = -\frac{9\pi}{14}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the quotient $u$ from the polar expressions:
$$u = \frac{2\mathrm{i}\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{7}\right)\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi}{7}\mathrm{i}}}{-2\mathrm{i}\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{14}\right)\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\pi}{14}\mathrm{i}}} = -\frac{\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{7}\right)}{\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{14}\right)}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{5\pi}{14}\mathrm{i}}$$

Extract modulus and incorporate negative sign for argument:
$$|u| = \frac{\sin(2\pi/7)}{\sin(\pi/14)}$$
$$\arg(u) = \frac{5\pi}{14} - \pi = -\frac{9\pi}{14}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Finding 4th roots of complex number via exponential form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Converting right-hand side to exponential form.
Finding all 4 roots and evaluating Cartesian form of special root.

walkthrough.text:
Find modulus and argument formula for roots:
$$r = 16^{1/4} = 2$$
$$\theta_k = \frac{-\frac{2\pi}{3} + 2k\pi}{4} = -\frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{k\pi}{2} \quad (k = 0, 1, 2, 3)$$

List the four roots in principal argument range:
$$w_1 = 2\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\pi}{6}\mathrm{i}}, \quad w_2 = 2\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\pi}{3}\mathrm{i}}, \quad w_3 = 2\mathrm{e}^{\frac{5\pi}{6}\mathrm{i}}, \quad w_4 = 2\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{2\pi}{3}\mathrm{i}}$$

Evaluate root with smallest positive argument ($\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}$):
$$w = 2\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} + \mathrm{i}\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 2\left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\mathrm{i}\right) = 1 + \sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}$$

hints: Since $OACB$ is a square, the diagonal bisects $\angle AOB = \pi/2$, so $\arg(z_C) = \arg(z_A) + \frac{\pi}{4}$.

walkthrough.text:
Use the square geometry formed by vectors $OA$ and $OB$:
$$\arg(z_C) = \arg(z_A) + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \arg(z_A) + \frac{\pi}{4}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Recognises square geometry to show diagonal angle $\arg(z_C) = \arg(z_A) + \frac{\pi}{4}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Verifying Cartesian slope via compound angle tangent.

hints: Verify that this equals the Cartesian gradient $\frac{7 - 0}{-1 - 0} = -7$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the compound angle formula for tangent:
$$\tan\left(\alpha + \frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\tan\alpha + \tan(\pi/4)}{1 - \tan\alpha\tan(\pi/4)} = \frac{\frac{4}{3} + 1}{1 - \frac{4}{3}(1)}$$
Confirm that the line from origin to $C(-1, 7)$ has gradient $\frac{7}{-1} = -7$.
